extracted.intended_audience: editors, journalists, media policy makers, and researchers working with public service broadcasters
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes editorial frameworks and newsworthiness criteria used by public service broadcasters (ABC Australia, CBC Canada, NHK Japan), including common principles, organization-specific rules, and what differentiates PSBs from commercial outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-partisan operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public service broadcasters must operate in a non-partisan manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs are expected to avoid partisan alignment or advocacy; editorial choices should not favor political actors. This is listed as a core common PSB principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve citizens, not advertisers; programming and editorial choices should prioritize public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs have an explicit duty to provide content that benefits the public sphere rather than commercial objectives. This underpins decisions to cover less-popular but important subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence from government
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain editorial independence despite government funding or oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs should safeguard newsrooms and editorial processes from political control or interference; independence is repeatedly emphasized as a principle even where boards are government-appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide balanced and impartial reporting across issues and political debates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should fairly present differing viewpoints and avoid systematic bias. Balance/impartiality is a recurring pillar across ABC, CBC, and NHK guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure truthful, accurate reporting and maintain journalistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-checking, verification, and integrity in sourcing are central. Codes of practice and journalistic handbooks emphasise accuracy as a foundational standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide broad coverage across domestic and international issues, not narrow or solely market-driven beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs are expected to cover a wide range of topics — local, national, and international — to inform citizens comprehensively rather than only high-rating content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of voices and perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure inclusion of diverse voices, regions, and perspectives in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates include representation across geographic regions, minority groups, and different perspectives; PSBs are expected to serve a pluralistic public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability to audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Be accountable to the public audience for editorial standards and mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms such as public hearings, standards committees, corrections, and transparent policies support accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABC: political independence as statutory organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: ABC is a politically independent statutory organisation despite having a government-appointed board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisational form is emphasised to underscore editorial independence; the existence of a government-appointed board does not override the editorial independence requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABC Code of Practice (accuracy, impartiality, fair dealing, privacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: ABC Code of Practice covers accuracy, impartiality, fair dealing and privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ABC-specific rules codify general PSB principles into concrete standards for editorial decisions, privacy handling, and fair treatment of subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABC Editorial Standards: independence, integrity, responsiveness, public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Four stated editorial standards guiding ABC journalism: independence, integrity, responsiveness and public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standards guide day-to-day editorial judgement and programming choices; 'responsiveness' implies listening to audience concerns and being responsive to complaints/feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABC programming obligations (breadth of content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required to provide news, current affairs, entertainment, drama, comedy, sport, music, arts and education programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory remit specifies a wide range of content types PSBs must deliver, supporting cultural and educational goals beyond news.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBC duty to provide consistent high-quality information
rubrics_metrics.description: CBC’s mandate: provide consistent, high-quality information "upon which all Canadians may rely."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty frames editorial priorities and sets an expectation of reliability and public trustworthiness for CBC content.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBC pillars: accuracy, fairness, balance, impartiality, integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: CBC Journalistic Policy Handbook pillars include accuracy, fairness, balance, impartiality and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pillars form the evaluative criteria for reporting and guide specific policies on sourcing, conflicts, and political coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBC specific guidance on sensitive practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on conflict of interest, anonymous sources, hidden cameras, reporting on children, reconstructions and political coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete procedural rules address when and how to use sensitive methods (e.g., anonymity, surreptitious filming), how to handle vulnerable subjects, and standards for reconstructions to avoid misleading the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBC public hearings on standards (accountability mechanism)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBC conducts public hearings on standards as part of accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public consultation and hearings are used to review and legitimise editorial standards and policies, enabling audience input.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHK truthful and accurate reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: NHK requires truthful and accurate reporting as a core guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHK's editorial rules reiterate accuracy and truthfulness as non-negotiable requirements for all reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHK fairness and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: NHK emphasises fair and impartial coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHK expects reporting to be free of bias and present multiple perspectives where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHK comprehensive domestic coverage (including local Japan)
rubrics_metrics.description: NHK is required to provide comprehensive coverage that includes local Japanese regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on reaching beyond metropolitan centers to reflect national diversity and local issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHK special attention to wartime memory
rubrics_metrics.description: NHK editorial guidelines include special attention to wartime memory in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical sensitivity and context are required when dealing with wartime topics, reflecting national memory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHK international broadcasting through NHK World
rubrics_metrics.description: NHK maintains international broadcasting (NHK World) to communicate Japanese perspectives globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International services are part of the remit to inform both domestic and global audiences about Japan and its interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: National significance as newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritise stories of national significance—what matters to the country as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs evaluate newsworthiness partly by national impact or relevance rather than purely individual or local interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse regional coverage requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure coverage of regions beyond metropolitan centres to reflect national diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocating resources to regional reporting prevents urban bias and ensures representation of remote/underserved areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: International events with national relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover international events selectively when they have clear relevance to the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs balance global reporting with its direct implications for domestic audiences, justifying foreign coverage by national relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural and educational value as justification for coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Include content for cultural enrichment and educational purposes even if not commercially lucrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs prioritise programs that contribute to cultural life and citizen education, including arts, languages and heritage programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on underserved communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Give attention to communities and topics underserved by commercial media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs should cover minority groups, linguistic communities, and topics that lack commercial appeal to promote inclusion and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive (not narrow) editorial remit
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a broad editorial remit rather than narrowing content to highest-demand niches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial strategies should aim for breadth across genres and subjects, ensuring public value coverage even when audience size is small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Less commercial pressure enables public-interest journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced reliance on ratings/advertising allows pursuit of important but less-popular stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs are expected to prioritise public interest over audience maximisation, supporting investigative reporting and long-form journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for democratic deliberation
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming and editorial decisions should support democratic debate and informed citizenry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs have an obligation to facilitate public discussion on civic matters, including hosting debates, explaining policy and providing platforms for civic voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate to cover unprofitable but important content
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation to provide coverage and programming that may be commercially unprofitable but socially important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes arts, minority languages, regional reporting, and investigative pieces that lack mass-market appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment in foreign bureaus and international reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: PSBs invest in foreign bureaus to provide independent international reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining overseas correspondents is highlighted as a public-value investment that commercial broadcasters may not sustain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment in cultural and educational programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial and editorial resources should support cultural and educational content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs justify allocating time and budget to content that fosters national culture, languages and knowledge, distinct from entertainment-driven scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on minority and indigenous languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide programming in minority and indigenous languages (examples: Welsh at BBC, Inuktitut at CBC, Ainu at NHK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language services are a concrete expression of PSB diversity and inclusion mandates, requiring resource allocation and specialized programming.
